trickyParts: The sweep's one real regression was guidance, not code: in the controller skill one sentence had been carrying both the server's refusal and the report's own length budget, so raising the number told every controller it may write a 32,000-character daily report to a person. The two facts are now separate, and the server's refusal is not restated there at all, since a report of a couple of thousand characters never meets it and a bare restatement would be the same conflation in a second sentence. skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md and docs/site/.../for-agents.md were read for the same conflation and have none: both state the server's cap plainly, under wording that says so.
Giving the report a budget took the controller skill to 501 lines, which pi-legion's skills guard refuses at 500. CI caught it; the paragraph was tightened to three lines rather than the guard moved.

An instruction softer than the proof that measures it is a defect in the instruction, not in the proof: scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh asserts the report is at most 2,000 characters inside until_true 300, whose timeout ends in fail, so a controller obeying "under about 2,000" with a 2,050-character report would burn 300 seconds and fail that row blaming a missing report. The wording is now hard; the assertion was left alone, because it is the only thing that measures the budget.
deviations: The reviewer's six minor findings were folded into this round rather than the named fast-follow, at the architect's ruling that a fast-follow pull request after the merge is work nobody in this tree owns. The PR body's `Fast-follow:` line is `none`.
No local run of any lane needing Docker, Postgres or a compiler: this pod has none, so those proofs are CI runs read from their logs and never claimed as local runs.

The margin's byte bounds are unchanged, as the architect accepted; this round documents the consequence and covers the anchored path, and adds no second full-cap reply to pin the 256 KiB record bound.

Round 2 is text only — no behaviour changed — but the code head moved, so every proof is re-cited at 042d4a7641662966166de1f5e65a90aba2dbe0f9 from the new jobs' own logs rather than carried across. The three thermonuclear findings the reviewer examined and did not hold (the GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT seam's shape, the splitting clause that quotes growth.go's own refusal wording, and the mixed overCapMessage/literal conventions in the two envoy-client test files) were left alone on the architect's ruling not to widen the round.
discoveredComplexity: A document's margin is bounded in bytes while the comment cap counts UTF-16 units, so the two budgets are spent in different currencies: one full-cap body is 32,000 bytes of ASCII and up to 96,000 of three-byte text. That asymmetry is why the consequence needed writing down rather than leaving to arithmetic.

Embedding cost per comment rises up to sixteenfold (embed.maxInputChars is 32,000 runes, about 8,000 estimated tokens against embedqueue's 200,000-per-minute budget). Escalated earlier and accepted with no work.

A 32,000-character agent turn is cut at AGENT_STREAM_LIMITS.partChars = 16,000 in the dashboard's Agent view. Delivery to the agent is unaffected, so AC3 still holds; the architect ruled it outside this issue.
